minutes.headline: Commission adopted certified-notice letters and $300/day fines to enforce unresolved wetland violations.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission heard two Eagle Scout project presentations (approved), worked through a full slate of wetland permit hearings including a contested after-the-fact violation case at 67 Island Road and a five-lot common driveway crossing wetlands on Northfield Road, and adopted a new enforcement policy of certified notices with daily fines for open violations. Several hearings were continued to August 6 pending peer review, site visits, or revised plans, and the board also approved its 2026 meeting schedule and discussed a restructured conservation/land-use budget.

what_happened.line: Commission adopted certified-notice letters and daily fines as its new tool for unresolved wetland violations.
A five-lot common driveway crossing wetlands on Northfield Road was sent to a paid peer review, at the applicant's cost, and continued to August 6.
A contested after-the-fact violation case on Island Road was continued to August 6 while an alternate remediation plan is prepared.
Two Eagle Scout projects and a tree-removal addition on Island Road were approved.
Open violations will now require a monthly status update to the commission until resolved.

why_it_matters: Anyone with an open wetland violation now faces a certified notice, a 30-day response window, and daily fines under the Wetlands Protection Act if it goes unresolved.
The Northfield Road common driveway and the Howard Street wetland-line dispute affect what can be built on those parcels; both return August 6 after outside review.
A restructured land-use budget has folded the conservation office's own line items into a shared department budget, changing how its spending gets reported going forward.
watch_next: August 6, 2025 hearing: Northfield Road driveway, Howard Street wetland delineation, Island Road violation remediation, and Lake Shirley
